Looking at the grid: a 4×4 square missing one corner cell has 15 squares, so each of the three equal pieces must have 5 squares.

**Checking the pieces:**
- **C (L-shape)** and **D (Y-shape)** each contain a straight line of 4 squares. Three such pieces would need three disjoint 4-lines in the grid, but the only 4-lines are the full rows 1–3 and columns 1–3; rows intersect columns, so only {rows 1,2,3} or {columns 1,2,3} work — and then the leftover squares (the stub row/column) cannot attach correctly to the ends of the lines. Impossible.
- **E (cross)** needs centers with all 4 neighbors inside; only centers in the middle 2×2 work, and any two of those overlap. Impossible.
- **B (U-shape)** cannot fill the corner structure of the truncated grid without leaving disconnected leftovers.
- **A (P-shape)** works: 
 - Piece 1: 2×2 block at top-left + cell below its left column. 
 - Piece 2: 2×2 block at top-right + cell below its right column. 
 - Piece 3: 2×2 block in the middle of the bottom row + cell to its left (the remaining bottom-left cell). 
 Each piece is a 2×3 rectangle missing one corner square — exactly figure A.

Thus one of the pieces is figure A.

\boxed{A}
